title.zh: 卷四十四 志第三十四 選舉志上
title.en: Volume 44 Treatises 39: Selecting and Appointing Officials 1
title.raw: 卷四十四 志第三十四 選舉志上 Volume 44 Treatises 39: Selecting and Appointing Officials 1

sentences.zh: 唐制，取士之科，多因隋舊，然其大要有三。

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations, the examination tracks for recruiting officials largely followed Sui precedents, yet their essential principles had three aspects.
translations.idiomatic: Tang rules for selecting officials drew mostly on Sui practice, but the system rested on three broad paths.

sentences.zh: 由學館者曰生徒，由州縣者曰鄉貢，皆升於有司而進退之。

translations.literal: Those coming through academies were called academy pupils; those coming through prefectures and counties were called village tribute candidates; all were advanced to the responsible offices, which promoted or rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from state schools were termed academy pupils; those nominated by prefectures and counties were village tribute entrants. Both were sent up to the responsible agencies, which decided who advanced and who was turned back.

sentences.zh: 其科之目，有秀才，有明經，有俊士，有進士，有明法，有明字，有明算，有一史，有三史，有開元禮，有道舉，有童子。

translations.literal: The categories of examinations included Xiucai, Mingjing, Junshi, Jinshi, Mingfa, Mingzi, Mingsuan, Yishi, Sanshi, Kaiyuan li, Daoju, and Tongzi.
translations.idiomatic: The examination subjects included Xiucai, Mingjing, Junshi, Jinshi, Mingfa (law), Mingzi (writing), Mingsuan (mathematics), single-history and triple-history tracks, Kaiyuan Rituals, Daoju (Daoist recommendation), and the child-prodigy Tongzi examination.

sentences.zh: 而明經之別，有五經，有三經，有二經，有學究一經，有三禮，有三傳，有史科。

translations.literal: Under Mingjing there were further divisions: Wujing, Sanjing, Erjing, Xuejiu yijing, Sanli, Sanzhuan, and the history examination.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingjing track in turn subdivided into five classics, three classics, two classics, single-classic specialist study, the three rites, the three commentaries, and the history examination.

sentences.zh: 此歲舉之常選也。

translations.literal: These were the regular selections held each year.
translations.idiomatic: These formed the routine annual recruitment cycle.

sentences.zh: 其天子自詔者曰制舉，所以待非常之才焉。

translations.literal: Those summoned by the Son of Heaven through his own edicts were called zhiju examinations, by which extraordinary talent was accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations proclaimed directly by the emperor were called zhiju (special summons), reserved for candidates of exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 凡學六，皆隸於國子監：國子學，生三百人，以文武三品以上子孫若從二品以上曾孫及勳官二品、縣公、京官四品帶三品勳封之子為之；

translations.literal: There were six schools in all, all subordinate to the Directorate of Education: the National University, with three hundred students, drawn from descendants of civil and military officials of the third rank and above, or great-grandsons of collateral second rank and above, and sons of merit officials of the second rank, county dukes, and capital officials of the fourth rank bearing third-rank merit titles and enfeoffments;
translations.idiomatic: Six schools in all fell under the Directorate of Education. The National University enrolled three hundred students: descendants of civil or military officials of third rank and above, great-grandsons in the collateral line of second rank and above, and sons of second-rank merit nobles, county dukes, and fourth-rank capital officials who carried third-rank merit titles and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 太學，生五百人，以五品以上子孫、職事官五品期親若三品曾孫及勳官三品以上有封之子為之；

translations.literal: the Imperial College, with five hundred students, drawn from descendants of officials of the fifth rank and above, close kin of fifth-rank active-duty officials or great-grandsons of third rank, and sons of merit officials of the third rank and above who held enfeoffments;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial College took five hundred students from descendants of fifth-rank officials and above, close relatives of fifth-rank active-duty officials or great-grandsons of third rank, and sons of enfeoffed merit officials of third rank and higher.

sentences.zh: 四門學，生千三百人，其五百人以勳官三品以上無封、四品有封及文武七品以上子為之，八百人以庶人之俊異者為之；

translations.literal: the Four Gates School, with thirteen hundred students, of whom five hundred were sons of unenfeoffed merit officials of the third rank and above, enfeoffed fourth-rank officials, and civil or military officials of the seventh rank and above, and eight hundred were outstanding commoners;
translations.idiomatic: The Four Gates School enrolled thirteen hundred: five hundred were sons of unenfeoffed third-rank merit nobles, enfeoffed fourth-rank officials, or civil and military officials of seventh rank and above; eight hundred were exceptionally talented commoners.

sentences.zh: 律學，生五十人，書學，生三十人，算學，生三十人，以八品以下子及庶人之通其學者為之。

translations.literal: the Law School with fifty students, the Calligraphy School with thirty, and the Mathematics School with thirty, drawn from sons of officials below the eighth rank and commoners who had mastered those disciplines.
translations.idiomatic: The Law School had fifty students; the Calligraphy and Mathematics Schools thirty each—sons of officials below eighth rank and commoners who had mastered those fields.

sentences.zh: 京都學生八十人，大都督、中都督府、上州各六十人，下都督府、中州各五十人，下州四十人，京縣五十人，上縣四十人，中縣、中下縣各三十五人，下縣二十人。

translations.literal: Capital district schools had eighty students; superior and middle area commands and upper prefectures sixty each; lower area commands and middle prefectures fifty; lower prefectures forty; capital counties fifty; upper counties forty; middle and lower-middle counties thirty-five each; lower counties twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment quotas ran: eighty in the capital district; sixty each in major and middle area commands and upper prefectures; fifty in lesser commands and middle prefectures; forty in lower prefectures; fifty in capital counties; forty in upper counties; thirty-five in middle and lower-middle counties; twenty in lower counties.

sentences.zh: 國子監生，尚書省補，祭酒統焉。

translations.literal: Students of the Directorate of Education were appointed by the Department of State Affairs and overseen by the Chancellor of the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students were appointed through the Department of State Affairs and placed under the Chancellor of the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 州縣學生，州縣長官補，長史主焉。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county students were appointed by prefectural and county chiefs and administered by the chief secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county students were enrolled by local chiefs and supervised by their chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 凡館二：門下省有弘文館，生三十人；

translations.literal: There were two academies: under the Secretariat was the Hongwen Academy, with thirty students;
translations.idiomatic: Two academies stood apart: the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, with thirty students;

sentences.zh: 東宮有崇文館，生二十人。

translations.literal: under the Eastern Palace was the Chongwen Academy, with twenty students.
translations.idiomatic: and the Chongwen Academy in the Eastern Palace, with twenty.

sentences.zh: 以皇緦麻以上親，皇太后、皇后大功以上親，宰相及散官一品、功臣身食實封者、京官職事從三品、中書黃門侍郎之子為之。

translations.literal: They were drawn from imperial kin within the zimao mourning grade and closer, kin of the empress dowager and empress within the dagong grade and closer, sons of chancellors and first-rank honorary officials, merit nobles receiving substantive enfeoffments, active capital officials of the third rank, junior assistant, and sons of Secretariat and Chancellery vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: Students were sons of imperial relatives within the zimao mourning circle, relatives of the empress dowager and empress within the dagong circle, chancellors and first-rank honorary officials, merit nobles on substantive fiefs, active third-rank capital officials, and sons of vice directors of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 凡博士、助教，分經授諸生，未終經者無易業。

translations.literal: Erudites and teaching assistants divided the classics among the students for instruction; those who had not finished a classic might not change their course of study.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites and assistants taught the classics by division; students could not switch subjects before completing a classic.

sentences.zh: 凡生，限年十四以上，十九以下；

translations.literal: Students in general were limited to ages fourteen through nineteen;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary students had to be between fourteen and nineteen;

sentences.zh: 律學十八以上，二十五以下。

translations.literal: law students from eighteen through twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: law students from eighteen through twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 凡《禮記》、《春秋左氏傳》為大經，《詩》、《周禮》、《儀禮》為中經，《易》、《尚書》、《春秋公羊傳》、《谷梁傳》為小經。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn were major classics; the Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites were middle classics; the Changes, Documents, Gongyang Commentary, and Guliang Commentary were minor classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Commentary ranked as major classics; the Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Etiquette and Rites as middle classics; the Changes, Documents, and the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries as minor classics.

sentences.zh: 通二經者，大經、小經各一，若中經二。

translations.literal: To master two classics required one major and one minor, or two middle classics.
translations.idiomatic: Mastery of two classics meant one major and one minor, or two middle classics.

sentences.zh: 通三經者，大經、中經、小經各一。

translations.literal: To master three required one each of major, middle, and minor.
translations.idiomatic: Three classics required one major, one middle, and one minor.

sentences.zh: 通五經者，大經皆通，餘經各一，《孝經》、《論語》皆兼通之。

translations.literal: To master five required all major classics plus one each of the remaining classics, with both the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects also mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Five classics meant all major texts plus one from each remaining group, with both the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects included.

sentences.zh: 凡治《孝經》、《論語》共限一歲，《尚書》、《公羊傳》、《谷梁傳》各一歲半，《易》、《詩》、《周禮》、《儀禮》各二歲，《禮記》、《左氏傳》各三歲。

translations.literal: Study of the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects together was limited to one year; the Documents, Gongyang, and Guliang each to one and a half years; the Changes, Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonial Rites each to two years; the Record of Rites and Zuo Commentary each to three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Piety Classic and Analects together took one year; Documents, Gongyang, and Guliang one and a half each; Changes, Odes, Rites of Zhou, and Etiquette two each; Record of Rites and Zuo Commentary three each.

sentences.zh: 學書，日紙一幅，間習時務策，讀《國語》、《說文》、《字林》、《三蒼》、《爾雅》。

translations.literal: Calligraphy students copied one sheet of paper daily, intermittently practiced current-affairs policy essays, and read the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphy students copied one sheet a day, practiced policy essays on current affairs from time to time, and studied the Discourses of the States, Shuowen, Zilin, Sancang, and Erya.

sentences.zh: 凡書學，石經三體限三歲，《說文》二歲，《字林》一歲。

translations.literal: For calligraphy study, the three stone-classic scripts were limited to three years, the Shuowen to two, and the Zilin to one.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphy training allotted three years for the three stone-classic scripts, two for the Shuowen, and one for the Zilin.

sentences.zh: 凡算學，《孫子》、《五曹》共限一歲，《九章》、《海島》共三歲，《張丘建》、《夏侯陽》各一歲，《周髀》、《五經算》共一歲，《綴術》四歲，《緝古》三歲，《記遺》、《三等數》皆兼習之。

translations.literal: For mathematics, Master Sun and Five Offices together one year; Nine Chapters and Sea Island together three years; Zhang Qiujian and Xiahou Yang each one year; Zhou Bi and Five Classics Mathematics together one year; Continuation Methods four years; Collation of Antiquity three years; with Memorial of Remainders and Third-Rank Numbers studied throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Mathematics curricula ran: Master Sun and Five Offices, one year together; Nine Chapters and Sea Island, three; Zhang Qiujian and Xiahou Yang, one each; Zhou Bi and Five Classics Mathematics, one together; Continuation Methods, four; Collation of Antiquity, three—with Memorial of Remainders and Third-Rank Numbers studied alongside throughout.

sentences.zh: 旬給假一日。

translations.literal: Each ten-day period granted one day of leave.
translations.idiomatic: Students received one day off every ten-day cycle.

sentences.zh: 前假，博士考試，讀者千言試一帖，帖三言，講者二千言問大義一條，總三條通二為第，不及者有罰。

translations.literal: Before leave, erudites examined them: readers were tested on one slip per thousand characters, each slip of three characters; lecturers were questioned on one major principle per two thousand characters; of three questions in all, passing two counted as a grade, with penalties for failure.
translations.idiomatic: Before holidays, erudites tested students: readers faced one character-slip per thousand characters read (three characters per slip); lecturers one question on major principles per two thousand characters. Passing two of three questions counted as success; failure brought punishment.

sentences.zh: 歲終，通一年之業，口問大義十條，通八為上，六為中，五為下。

translations.literal: At year's end, having completed the year's course, they were orally questioned on ten major principles; passing eight ranked upper, six middle, five lower.
translations.idiomatic: At year-end, after completing the annual curriculum, students answered ten oral questions on major principles: eight passes ranked upper, six middle, five lower.

sentences.zh: 並三下與在學九歲、律生六歲不堪貢者罷歸。

translations.literal: Those with three lower grades together, or who after nine years in school or six as law students were unfit for tribute presentation, were dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Students with three lower grades, or who after nine years (six for law students) still could not qualify for presentation, were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 諸學生通二經、俊士通三經已及第而願留者，四門學生補太學，太學生補國子學。

translations.literal: Students who had passed two classics, or Junshi who had passed three and wished to remain, were promoted from the Four Gates to the Imperial College, and Imperial College students to the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Students who had passed two classics, or Junshi who passed three and wished to stay on, advanced from Four Gates to Imperial College, and from Imperial College to the National University.

sentences.zh: 每歲五月有田假，九月有授衣假，二百里外給程。

translations.literal: Each year in the fifth month there was field-work leave; in the ninth month, garment-distribution leave; those beyond two hundred li were granted travel time.
translations.idiomatic: Each year May brought field-work leave and September garment leave; students living more than two hundred li away received travel time.

sentences.zh: 其不帥教及歲中違程滿三十日，事故百日，緣親病二百日，皆罷歸。

translations.literal: Those who did not follow instruction, or within the year exceeded permitted absence by thirty days, or by one hundred for official business, or two hundred for parental illness, were all dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Students who defied instruction, or were absent thirty days without leave, one hundred for official duties, or two hundred for a parent's illness, were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既罷，條其狀下之屬所，五品以上子孫送兵部，准廕配色。

translations.literal: Once dismissed, their circumstances were recorded and sent down to the subordinate office; descendants of fifth rank and above were sent to the Ministry of War for yin privilege assignment of colors.
translations.idiomatic: On dismissal, their records went to the appropriate office; descendants of fifth rank and above were referred to the Ministry of War for hereditary privilege and uniform-color assignment.

sentences.zh: 每歲仲冬，州、縣、館、監舉其成者送之尚書省；

translations.literal: Each year in mid-winter, prefectures, counties, academies, and directorates presented their graduates and sent them to the Department of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Each midwinter, prefectures, counties, academies, and the Directorate presented their graduates to the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 而舉選不繇館、學者，謂之鄉貢，皆懷牒自列於州、縣。

translations.literal: those seeking selection who did not come through academies or schools were called village tribute candidates; all carried their credentials and presented themselves at prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: candidates who did not come through schools were village tribute entrants, each presenting credentials at their prefecture or county.

sentences.zh: 試已，長吏以鄉飲酒禮，會屬僚，設賓主，陳俎豆，備管弦，牲用少牢，歌《鹿鳴》之詩，因與耆艾敘長少焉。

translations.literal: After the examination, the chief official held the village drinking ceremony, gathering subordinate officials, setting host and guest, displaying meat and grain offerings, providing strings and winds, using the lesser pen sacrifice, singing the Deer Cry poem, and thereby with elders ordering senior and junior.
translations.idiomatic: After the tests, local chiefs held the village drinking rite with their staff—host and guest seated, offerings set out, music provided, a lesser pen sacrifice, the "Deer Cry" sung, and elders and juniors seated by age.

sentences.zh: 既至省，皆疏名列到，結款通保及所居，始由戶部集閱，而關於考功員外郎試之。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital department, all listed their names in memorials upon arrival, made sworn bonds of mutual guarantee and residence, were first assembled and reviewed by the Ministry of Revenue, then referred to the Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel for examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital, candidates registered by memorial, filed mutual guarantees and addresses, passed Revenue Ministry review, and were examined by the Vice Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凡秀才，試方略策五道，以文理通粗為上上、上中、上下、中上，凡四等為及第。

translations.literal: For Xiucai, five policy-strategy questions were tested; literary reasoning from refined to coarse ranked upper-upper, upper-middle, upper-lower, and middle-upper—four grades in all counted as passing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucai candidates answered five policy-strategy questions; four grades from upper-upper through middle-upper, judged on literary clarity, counted as passing.

sentences.zh: 凡明經，先帖文，然後口試，經問大義十條，答時務策三道，亦為四等。

translations.literal: For Mingjing, text-slips came first, then oral examination: ten questions on major principles of the classics, three current-affairs policy answers—also four grades.
translations.idiomatic: Mingjing candidates first took text-slips, then oral exams: ten questions on classical principles and three policy essays, again graded in four ranks.

sentences.zh: 凡《開元禮》，通大義百條、策三道者，超資與官；

translations.literal: For Kaiyuan Rituals, those passing one hundred major principles and three policy questions received extraordinary qualification and office;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan Rituals, passing one hundred principle questions and three policy essays brought extraordinary promotion and appointment;

sentences.zh: 義通七十、策通二者，及第。

translations.literal: passing seventy on principles and two on policy counted as passing the examination.
translations.idiomatic: seventy principles and two policy essays sufficed to pass.

sentences.zh: 散、試官能通者，依正員。

translations.literal: Honorary and probationary officials who could pass were treated like regular appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary and probationary officials who passed were treated like regular appointees.

sentences.zh: 凡三傳科，《左氏傳》問大義五十條，《公羊》、《谷梁傳》三十條，策皆三道，義通七以上、策通二以上為第，白身視五經，有出身及前資官視學究一經。

translations.literal: For the three-commentaries examination, fifty major questions on the Zuo Commentary, thirty each on Gongyang and Guliang, three policy questions for all; passing seven-tenths on principles and two-tenths on policy ranked as a grade; commoners were treated like Wujing, those with examination credentials or prior office like Xuejiu yijing.
translations.idiomatic: The three-commentaries track tested fifty Zuo questions, thirty each on Gongyang and Guliang, plus three policy essays; seven-tenths on principles and two on policy passed. Commoners were ranked like five-classics graduates; those with credentials or prior office like single-classic specialists.

sentences.zh: 凡史科，每史問大義百條、策三道，義通七、策通二以上為第。

translations.literal: For the history examination, each history had one hundred major questions and three policy questions; passing seven-tenths on principles and two on policy ranked as a grade.
translations.idiomatic: The history track set one hundred principle questions and three policy essays per history; seven-tenths on principles and two on policy constituted a pass.

sentences.zh: 能通一史者，白身視五經、三傳，有出身及前資官視學究一經；

translations.literal: those mastering one history were treated like Wujing or Sanzhuan for commoners, or Xuejiu yijing for those with credentials or prior office;
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed one history ranked commoners like five-classics or three-commentaries graduates, and credentialed candidates like single-classic specialists;

sentences.zh: 三史皆通者，獎擢之。

translations.literal: those passing all three histories received special commendation and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: those who passed all three histories received special commendation and advancement.

sentences.zh: 凡童子科，十歲以下能通一經及《孝經》、《論語》，卷誦文十，通者予官；

translations.literal: For the child-prodigy examination, those under ten who could master one classic plus the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects, reciting ten passages from a scroll—all passing received office;
translations.idiomatic: The child-prodigy track admitted those under ten who mastered one classic plus the Filial Piety Classic and Analects, reciting ten passages—full passers received office;

sentences.zh: 通七，予出身。

translations.literal: passing seven granted examination credentials.
translations.idiomatic: passing seven passages granted examination credentials.

sentences.zh: 凡進士，試時務策五道、帖一大經，經、策全通為甲第；

translations.literal: For Jinshi, five current-affairs policy questions and one major classic text-slip were tested; full passage on both classics and policy ranked first class;
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi candidates took five policy essays and one major-classic text-slip; passing both fully earned first class;

sentences.zh: 策通四、帖過四以上為乙第。

translations.literal: passing four policy questions and more than four on text-slips ranked second class.
translations.idiomatic: four policy passes and more than four text-slip passes earned second class.

sentences.zh: 凡明法，試律七條、令三條，全通為甲第，通八為乙第。

translations.literal: For Mingfa, seven statutes and three ordinances were tested; full passage ranked first class, passing eight ranked second.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfa tested seven statute articles and three ordinance articles; all ten passed for first class, eight for second.

sentences.zh: 凡書學，先口試，通，乃墨試《說文》、《字林》二十條，通十八為第。

translations.literal: For calligraphy, oral examination came first; on passing, written examination on twenty items from the Shuowen and Zilin—passing eighteen ranked as a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphy candidates took an oral test first, then a written test on twenty Shuowen and Zilin items—eighteen passes constituted a grade.

sentences.zh: 凡算學，錄大義本條為問答，明數造術，詳明術理，然後為通。

translations.literal: For mathematics, major principles were recorded item by item as questions and answers; clarity in numbers, construction of methods, and detailed exposition of method-principles—only then counted as passing.
translations.idiomatic: Mathematics exams recorded major principles as Q&A; candidates had to demonstrate numerical clarity, method construction, and thorough explanation of method—these together constituted a pass.

sentences.zh: 試《九章》三條、《海島》《孫子》《五曹》《張丘建》《夏侯陽》《周髀》《五經算》各一條，十通六，《記遺》、《三等數》帖讀十得九，為第。

translations.literal: Three items from the Nine Chapters, one each from Sea Island, Master Sun, Five Offices, Zhang Qiujian, Xiahou Yang, Zhou Bi, and Five Classics Mathematics were tested; of ten, passing six; for Memorial of Remainders and Third-Rank Numbers, ten text-slips with nine correct ranked as a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Tests drew three Nine Chapters problems and one each from seven other texts; six of ten had to pass. Memorial of Remainders and Third-Rank Numbers required nine of ten text-slips correct for a grade.

sentences.zh: 試《綴術》、《輯古》，錄大義為問答者，明數造術，詳明術理，無注者合數造術，不失義理，然後為通。

translations.literal: For Continuation Methods and Collation of Antiquity, those recording major principles as Q&A had to show clarity in numbers and method-construction, detailed method-principles; where there were no annotations, combining numbers to construct methods without losing principle—only then counted as passing.
translations.idiomatic: Continuation Methods and Collation of Antiquity required Q&A on major principles, clear numeracy and method-building, and sound reasoning—even without commentaries, methods had to be constructed correctly.

sentences.zh: 《綴術》七條、《輯古》三條，十通六，《記遺》、《三等數》帖讀十得九，為第。

translations.literal: Seven items from Continuation Methods and three from Collation of Antiquity—of ten, passing six; Memorial of Remainders and Third-Rank Numbers, ten text-slips with nine correct ranked as a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Continuation Methods and three Collation of Antiquity items were tested—six of ten to pass; nine of ten text-slips on the other two texts also sufficed.

sentences.zh: 落經者，雖通六，不第。

translations.literal: Those who failed the classic portion, though passing six overall, did not rank.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who failed the classics section did not pass even if they cleared six other items.

sentences.zh: 凡弘文、崇文生，試一大經、一小經，或二中經，或《史記》、《前後漢書》、《三國志》各一，或時務策五道。

translations.literal: Hongwen and Chongwen students were tested on one major and one minor classic, or two middle classics, or one each of the Records of the Grand Historian, Book of Han, Book of Later Han, and Records of the Three Kingdoms, or five current-affairs policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen and Chongwen students took one major and one minor classic, two middle classics, one volume each from four standard histories, or five policy essays.

sentences.zh: 經史皆試策十道。

translations.literal: For classics and histories alike, ten policy questions were tested.
translations.idiomatic: Classic and history tracks both required ten policy questions.

sentences.zh: 經通六，史及時務策通三，皆帖《孝經》、《論語》共十條通六，為第。

translations.literal: Passing six on classics, three on history or current-affairs policy, and six of ten combined text-slips on the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects ranked as a grade.
translations.idiomatic: A pass required six classic questions, three history or policy questions, and six of ten combined Filial Piety and Analects text-slips.

sentences.zh: 凡貢舉非其人者、廢舉者、校試不以實者，皆有罰。

translations.literal: Presenting unworthy candidates, abandoning presentation, or examining without truth—all incurred penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who presented unfit candidates, failed to present qualified ones, or graded exams dishonestly faced punishment.

sentences.zh: 其教人取士著於令者，大略如此。

translations.literal: The regulations on educating people and recruiting officials were broadly as stated above.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory rules for educating talent and selecting officials followed this general outline.

sentences.zh: 而士之進取之方，與上之好惡、所以育材養士、招來獎進之意，有司選士之法，因時增損不同。

translations.literal: Yet the means by which scholars advanced, the ruler's preferences, the intent to nurture talent and cultivate scholars, attract and reward advancement, and the methods of responsible offices in selecting scholars—all varied with additions and reductions according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet how scholars advanced, what emperors favored, how the court meant to cultivate and recruit talent, and how officials selected candidates—all shifted with the times.

sentences.zh: 自高祖初入長安，開大丞相府，下令置生員，自京師至於州縣皆有數。

translations.literal: From when Gaozu first entered Chang'an, he opened the Grand Chancellor's Office and ordered student quotas set, with fixed numbers from the capital down to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first entered Chang'an, he opened the Grand Chancellor's Office and ordered student quotas for the capital and every prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 既即位，又詔秘書外省別立小學，以教宗室子孫及功臣子弟。

translations.literal: After taking the throne, he also ordered a separate elementary school established at the outer Secretariat to teach imperial clan descendants and sons of merit officials.
translations.idiomatic: After his enthronement, he ordered a separate elementary school at the outer Secretariat for imperial clansmen and sons of meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 其後又詔諸州明經、秀才、俊士、進士明于理體為鄉里稱者，縣考試，州長重覆，歲隨方物入貢；

translations.literal: Later he also ordered that in all prefectures, Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi candidates clear in principle and structure and praised in their villages be examined by counties and re-examined by prefectural chiefs, entering tribute yearly with local products;
translations.idiomatic: He later ordered prefectures to examine locally renowned Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi candidates at the county level, with prefects re-examining them and sending them to court each year with regional tribute;

sentences.zh: 吏民子弟學藝者，皆送於京學，為設考課之法。

translations.literal: sons of officials and commoners studying arts were all sent to the capital schools, for which examination methods were established.
translations.idiomatic: officials' sons and commoners studying the arts were sent to capital schools with formal examination rules.

sentences.zh: 州、縣、鄉皆置學焉。

translations.literal: Schools were established in prefectures, counties, and townships alike.
translations.idiomatic: Schools were set up in prefectures, counties, and townships throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，益崇儒術。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Confucian learning was further honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, he elevated Confucian learning still further.

sentences.zh: 乃于門下別置弘文館，又增置書、律學，進士加讀經、史一部。

translations.literal: He then separately established the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, added calligraphy and law schools, and required Jinshi candidates to read an additional classic or history.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Hongwen Academy under the Secretariat, added calligraphy and law schools, and required Jinshi candidates to study an extra classic or history.

sentences.zh: 十三年，東宮置崇文館。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Eastern Palace established the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirteenth year, the Eastern Palace gained the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 自天下初定，增築學舍至千二百區，雖七營飛騎，亦置生，遣博士為授經。

translations.literal: From the time the realm was first pacified, school buildings were increased to twelve hundred wards; even the seven camps of flying cavalry had students placed, with erudites sent to teach the classics.
translations.idiomatic: After the empire was pacified, school buildings rose to twelve hundred; even the seven flying-cavalry camps enrolled students and received erudites to teach the classics.

sentences.zh: 四夷若高麗、百濟、新羅、高昌、吐蕃，相繼遣子弟入學，遂至八千餘人。

translations.literal: Foreign peoples such as Koguryŏ, Paekche, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent sons in succession to study, until there were more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: States such as Koguryŏ, Paekche, Silla, Gaochang, and Tibet sent princes and sons to study in succession, until enrollment exceeded eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年，始停秀才科。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui under Gaozong, the Xiucai examination was first suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui year 2 of Gaozong, the Xiucai examination was abolished.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，東都置國子監，明年以書學隸蘭台，算學隸秘閣，律學隸詳刑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Directorate of Education was established in the eastern capital; the next year calligraphy was placed under the Orchid Terrace, mathematics under the Secret Archive, and law under Detailed Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo year 2, a Directorate of Education was set up in the eastern capital; the next year calligraphy moved under the Orchid Terrace, mathematics under the Secret Archive, and law under Detailed Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，加試貢士《老子》策，明經二條，進士三條。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, tribute scholars were additionally tested on Laozi policy questions—two for Mingjing, three for Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan year 2, tribute candidates faced added Laozi policy questions—two for Mingjing, three for Jinshi.

sentences.zh: 國子監置大成二十人，取已及第而聰明者為之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Education established twenty Senior Accomplished Scholars, drawn from those who had already passed examinations and were gifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate appointed twenty Senior Accomplished Scholars from examination graduates who showed exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 試書日誦千言，並日試策，所業十通七，然後補其祿俸，同直官。

translations.literal: They were tested in calligraphy by reciting one thousand characters daily, with daily policy tests as well; of ten subjects, passing seven—only then were salaries supplemented, equal to duty officers.
translations.idiomatic: They recited one thousand characters daily in calligraphy tests and took daily policy exams; passing seven of ten subjects earned salary supplementation equal to duty officers.

sentences.zh: 通四經業成，上于尚書，吏部試之，登第者加一階放選。

translations.literal: When four classics were mastered and studies completed, they were reported to the Department of State Affairs; the Ministry of Personnel examined them, and those passing received one rank added and release for selection.
translations.idiomatic: After mastering four classics, they were reported to the Department of State Affairs; the Ministry of Personnel examined them, and passers gained one rank and release for appointment.

sentences.zh: 其不第則習業如初，三歲而又試，三試而不中第，從常調。

translations.literal: Those who did not pass resumed study as before; after three years they were tested again; after three failures to pass, they followed regular rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Failures resumed study; after three years they were retested; three failures sent them into regular bureaucratic rotation.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，考功員外郎劉思立建言，明經多抄義條，進士唯誦舊策，皆亡實才，而有司以人數充第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, Vice Director of Personnel Liu Sili memorialized that Mingjing candidates mostly copied principle entries, Jinshi merely recited old policy answers—all lacked real talent, yet responsible offices filled quotas by head count.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong year 2, Vice Director Liu Sili warned that Mingjing candidates copied textbook entries, Jinshi memorized old essays—neither showed real ability—yet examiners filled quotas by head count.

sentences.zh: 乃詔自今明經試帖粗十得六以上，進士試雜文二篇，通文律者然後試策。

translations.literal: An edict therefore ordered that from then on Mingjing text-slips required six of ten coarse passages; Jinshi were tested on two belles-lettres pieces, and only after passing literary rules were policy questions given.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Mingjing candidates to pass six of ten text-slips, Jinshi to submit two belles-lettres pieces and take policy exams only after passing literary standards.

sentences.zh: 武后之亂，改易舊制頗多。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, old institutions were changed in considerable measure.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, the old examination system was altered extensively.

sentences.zh: 中宗反正，詔宗室三等以下、五等以上未出身，願宿衛及任國子生，聽之。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong restored proper rule, he ordered that imperial clansmen of the third rank and below and fifth rank and above who lacked examination credentials, if willing to serve as palace guards or enroll as Directorate students, were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong's restoration, imperial clansmen of third rank and below or fifth rank and above without credentials could serve as palace guards or enroll as Directorate students if they wished.

sentences.zh: 其家居業成而堪貢者，宗正寺試，送監舉如常法。

translations.literal: Those studying at home who completed their course and were fit for tribute presentation were examined by the Imperial Clan Court and sent to the Directorate for presentation by regular methods.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen who completed home study and qualified for presentation were examined by the Imperial Clan Court and sent to the Directorate by the usual process.

sentences.zh: 三衛番下日，願入學者，聽附國子學、太學及律館習業。

translations.literal: On days when the Three Guards rotated off duty, those wishing to enter study were permitted to attach to the National University, Imperial College, and law schools for coursework.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Guards rotated off duty, guards who wished to study could attach to the National University, Imperial College, or law schools.

sentences.zh: 蕃王及可汗子孫願入學者，附國子學讀書。

translations.literal: Foreign kings and khans' descendants who wished to study were permitted to attach to the National University for reading.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of foreign kings and khans who wished to study enrolled at the National University.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元五年，始令鄉貢明經、進士見訖，國子監謁先師，學官開講問義，有司為具食，清資五品以上官及朝集使皆往閱禮焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong, village-tribute Mingjing and Jinshi candidates, after their audience concluded, were first ordered to pay respects to the former master at the Directorate, with academic officers opening lectures to question principles; responsible offices provided food; pure-capital officials of the fifth rank and above and assembly envoys all went to observe the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 5, Xuanzong required village-tribute Mingjing and Jinshi, after their audience, to worship the sage at the Directorate while erudites lectured on principles; officials provided a feast, and fifth-rank pure-capital officials and assembly envoys attended the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 七年，又令弘文、崇文、國子生季一朝參。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Hongwen, Chongwen, and Directorate students were also ordered to attend court once each season.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Hongwen, Chongwen, and Directorate students were required to attend court once per season.

sentences.zh: 及注《老子道德經》成，詔天下家藏其書，貢舉人滅《尚書》、《論語》策，而加試《老子》。

translations.literal: When the annotated Laozi Daodejing was completed, an edict ordered every household in the realm to keep a copy; tribute candidates had Documents and Analects policy questions reduced and Laozi added to the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong finished his commentary on the Daodejing, he ordered every household to keep a copy, reduced Documents and Analects questions for tribute candidates, and added Laozi to the exams.

sentences.zh: 又敕州縣學生年二十五以下、八品子若庶人二十一以下通一經及未通經而聰悟有文辭、史學者，入四門學為俊士。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that prefectural and county students twenty-five and under, sons of eighth-rank officials or commoners twenty-one and under who had mastered one classic, or who had not mastered a classic but were gifted in literary composition and historical learning, enter the Four Gates School as Junshi.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered prefectural students under twenty-five, and eighth-rank sons or commoners under twenty-one who had mastered one classic—or showed literary and historical talent without a full classic—to enter Four Gates as Junshi.

sentences.zh: 即諸州貢舉省試不第，願入學者亦聽。

translations.literal: Those from all prefectures who failed the provincial tribute examination but wished to enter study were also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who failed the provincial examination but wished to study were also admitted.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，考功員外郎李昂為舉人詆訶，帝以員外郎望輕，遂移貢舉於禮部，以侍郎主之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Vice Director of Personnel Li Ang was reviled by candidates; the emperor considered the vice directorship too light in standing, and therefore moved tribute selection to the Ministry of Rites, with a vice minister presiding.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, candidates abused Vice Director Li Ang; deeming that post too low in rank, the emperor transferred examinations to the Ministry of Rites under a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 禮部選士自此始。

translations.literal: Selection of scholars by the Ministry of Rites began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From this point, the Ministry of Rites oversaw civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，始置崇玄學，習《老子》、《莊子》、《文子》、《列子》，亦曰道舉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Chongxuan School was first established to study the Laozi, Zhuangzi, Wenzi, and Liezi—also called the Daoist recommendation track.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, the Chongxuan School was founded for Laozi, Zhuangzi, Wenzi, and Liezi—the Daoist recommendation track.

sentences.zh: 其生，京、都各百人，諸州無常員。

translations.literal: Its students numbered one hundred each in the two capitals; prefectures had no fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment was one hundred in each capital; prefectures had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 官秩、廕第同國子，舉送、課試如明經。

translations.literal: Official rank and yin precedence were the same as the National University; presentation and course examinations followed Mingjing.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and hereditary privilege matched the National University; presentation and testing followed Mingjing rules.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，置廣文館于國學，以領生徒為進士者。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao, the Guangwen Academy was established within the state schools to oversee students preparing for the Jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 9, the Guangwen Academy was set up within the state schools to supervise Jinshi candidates.

sentences.zh: 舉人舊重兩監，後世祿者以京兆、同、華為榮，而不入學。

translations.literal: Candidates formerly valued the two directorates; later generations seeking office took glory in Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua prefectures and did not enter schools.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates once prized enrollment in the two directorates, but later office-seekers took prestige from Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua and skipped school entirely.

sentences.zh: 十二載，乃敕天下罷鄉貢，舉人不由國子及郡、縣學者，勿舉送。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict ordered the realm to suspend village tribute; candidates not coming through the Directorate or prefectural and county schools were not to be presented.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, the court suspended village tribute nationwide and barred presentation of candidates who had not come through the Directorate or local schools.

sentences.zh: 是歲，道舉停《老子》，加《周易》。

translations.literal: That year, the Daoist recommendation track suspended the Laozi and added the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Daoist track dropped Laozi and added the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 十四載，復鄉貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, village tribute was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, village tribute was restored.

sentences.zh: 代宗廣德二年，詔曰：「古者設太學，教胄子，雖年穀不登，兵革或動，而俎豆之事不廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde under Daizong, an edict stated: "In antiquity the Imperial College was established to teach the emperor's sons; though harvests failed or arms were raised, the rites of sacrifice were not abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde year 2, Daizong decreed: "Antiquity established the Imperial College to educate imperial heirs; even when harvests failed or war broke out, sacrificial rites were not abandoned."

sentences.zh: 頃年戎車屢駕，諸生輟講，宜追學生在館習業，度支給廚米。

translations.literal: In recent years war-chariots have been driven repeatedly and students have ceased lectures; students in the academies should be recalled to resume study, with the Department of Revenue supplying kitchen grain.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years repeated campaigns had halted instruction; students should return to the academies, with the Revenue Department supplying grain for their kitchens.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，賈至為侍郎，建言歲方艱歉，舉人赴省者，兩都試之。

translations.literal: " That year, Jia Zhi as vice minister memorialized that since the year was hard and lean, candidates traveling to the capital should be examined in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: " That year Vice Minister Jia Zhi proposed that, given famine conditions, candidates bound for the capital be examined in both capitals instead.

sentences.zh: 兩都試人自此始。

translations.literal: Examination of candidates in both capitals began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: Dual-capital examinations began at this point.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，詔習《開元禮》者舉同一經例，明經習律以代《爾雅》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, it was ordered that those studying Kaiyuan Rituals be presented by the same rules as one classic; Mingjing candidates studied statutes in place of the Erya.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year 2, Kaiyuan Rituals candidates followed single-classic presentation rules, and Mingjing students studied law codes instead of the Erya.

sentences.zh: 是時弘文、崇文生未補者，務取員闕以補，速於登第，而用廕乖實，至有假市門資、變易昭穆及假人試藝者。

translations.literal: At this time Hongwen and Chongwen students not yet appointed strove to fill vacant quotas for quick passage of examinations; yin privilege was used contrary to fact, until some falsely purchased market-gate credentials, altered lineage seniority, or had others take the arts examination for them.
translations.idiomatic: Unplaced Hongwen and Chongwen students rushed to fill vacant slots and pass quickly; hereditary privilege was abused—some bought credentials, falsified lineage, or sent proxies to take exams.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔宜據式考試，假代者論如法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that examinations follow the regulations; substitutes were to be prosecuted according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, the court required exams to follow regulations and punished proxy test-takers by law.

sentences.zh: 初，禮部侍郎親故移試考功，謂之別頭。

translations.literal: Initially, relatives and associates of the Vice Minister of Rites were transferred for examination to the Ministry of Personnel—called separate-track testing.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, the vice minister's kin and associates were examined separately by Personnel—called the "separate head" examination.

sentences.zh: 十六年，中書舍人高郢奏罷，議者是之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Secretariat Drafter Gao Ying memorialized to abolish it; discussants approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, Secretariat Drafter Gao Ying petitioned to abolish it, and critics agreed.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，置東都監生一百員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, one hundred Directorate students were established in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 2, the eastern capital received one hundred Directorate student slots.

sentences.zh: 然自天寶後，學校益廢，生徒流散。

translations.literal: Yet from after Tianbao, schools were increasingly abandoned and students scattered.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianbao, however, schools fell into disuse and students dispersed.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，雖置西監生，而館無定員。

translations.literal: In the Yongtai era, though western-capital Directorate students were established, the academies had no fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongtai, western-capital Directorate students were added, but academies still lacked fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 於是始定生員：西京國子館生八十人，太學七十人，四門三百人，廣文六十人，律館二十人，書、算館各十人；

translations.literal: Thereupon student quotas were first fixed: in the western capital, National University eighty, Imperial College seventy, Four Gates three hundred, Guangwen sixty, Law School twenty, Calligraphy and Mathematics ten each;
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were then fixed for the western capital: National University 80, Imperial College 70, Four Gates 300, Guangwen 60, Law 20, Calligraphy and Mathematics 10 each;

sentences.zh: 東都國子館十人，太學十五人，四門五十人，廣文十人，律館十人，書館三人，算館二人而已。

translations.literal: in the eastern capital, National University ten, Imperial College fifteen, Four Gates fifty, Guangwen ten, Law ten, Calligraphy three, Mathematics two only.
translations.idiomatic: the eastern capital had only 10, 15, 50, 10, 10, 3, and 2 respectively.

sentences.zh: 明經停口義，復試墨義十條。

translations.literal: Mingjing suspended oral interpretation and restored written principle examinations of ten items.
translations.idiomatic: Mingjing dropped oral interpretation and restored ten written principle questions.

sentences.zh: 五經取通五，明經通六。

translations.literal: Wujing required passing five; Mingjing required passing six.
translations.idiomatic: Five-classics candidates had to pass five; Mingjing candidates six.

sentences.zh: 其嘗坐法及為州縣小吏，雖藝文可采，勿舉。

translations.literal: Those who had been punished by law or served as petty officials in prefectures and counties, though their literary arts might be acceptable, were not to be presented.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates with criminal records or service as petty local officials were not presented, however talented their writing.

sentences.zh: 十三年，權知禮部侍郎庾承宣奏復考功別頭試。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Acting Vice Minister of Rites Yu Chengxuan memorialized to restore the Personnel separate-track examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, Acting Vice Minister Yu Chengxuan restored the Personnel separate-track exam.

sentences.zh: 初，開元中，禮部考試畢，送中書門下詳覆，其後中廢。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Kaiyuan era, after the Ministry of Rites examination concluded, results were sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery for detailed review; later this was suspended midway.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, after Rites exams finished, results went to the Secretariat and Chancellery for review—later discontinued.

sentences.zh: 是歲，侍郎錢徽所舉送，覆試多不中選，由是貶官，而舉人雜文復送中書門下。

translations.literal: That year, Vice Minister Qian Hui's presentations, upon re-examination, mostly failed selection; therefore he was demoted, and candidates' belles-lettres were again sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: That year Vice Minister Qian Hui's nominees mostly failed re-examination; he was demoted, and candidates' essays again went to the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，侍郎王起言：「故事，禮部已放榜，而中書門下始詳覆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changqing, Vice Minister Wang Qi stated: "By precedent, the Ministry of Rites had already posted the list, and only then did the Secretariat and Chancellery begin detailed review."
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing year 3, Vice Minister Wang Qi said: "By precedent, Rites posted results first, and only then did the Secretariat and Chancellery review them."

sentences.zh: 今請先詳覆，而後放榜。

translations.literal: " Now I request detailed review first, and posting the list afterward."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that review come first and posting afterward."

sentences.zh: 」議者以起雖避嫌，然失貢職矣。

translations.literal: " Critics held that though Wang Qi avoided suspicion, he had failed his duty in presenting tribute talent.
translations.idiomatic: " Critics said Wang Qi avoided conflict of interest but neglected his duty to present talent.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫殷侑言：「《三史》為書，勸善懲惡，亞於《六經》。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Yin You stated: "The Three Histories as books encourage good and punish evil, second only to the Six Classics."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Yin You said: "The Three Histories encourage virtue and punish vice, ranking just below the Six Classics."

sentences.zh: 比來史學都廢，至有身處班列，而朝廷舊章莫能知者。

translations.literal: Recently historical studies have all been abandoned, until some who stand in court ranks cannot know the old regulations of the court."
translations.idiomatic: Historical study has lapsed so far that officials in court ranks no longer know the dynasty's own precedents."

sentences.zh: 」於是立史科及三傳科。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the history examination and three-commentaries examination were established.
translations.idiomatic: " The history and three-commentaries examinations were then established.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，高鍇為考功員外郎，取士有不當，監察御史姚中立又奏停考功別頭試。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, Gao Kai as Vice Director of Personnel selected scholars improperly; Censor Yao Zhongli again memorialized to suspend the Personnel separate-track examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe year 3, Vice Director Gao Kai selected candidates improperly; Censor Yao Zhongli again petitioned to end the Personnel separate-track exam.

sentences.zh: 六年，侍郎賈餗又奏復之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Minister Jia Su again memorialized to restore it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Vice Minister Jia Su restored it again.

sentences.zh: 八年，宰相王涯以為「禮部取士，乃先以榜示中書，非至公之道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Chancellor Wang Ya held that "the Ministry of Rites selecting scholars by first showing the list to the Secretariat is not the way of utmost fairness."
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Chancellor Wang Ya argued that showing Rites examination results to the Secretariat first was not fully fair.

sentences.zh: 自今一委有司，以所試雜文、鄉貫、三代名諱送中書門下」。

translations.literal: " From now on let it be entirely entrusted to the responsible offices; send the belles-lettres examined, native place, and three generations of names and taboos to the Secretariat and Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth responsible offices alone should send examined essays, native place, and three generations of names and taboos to the Secretariat and Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 大抵眾科之目，進士尤為貴，其得人亦最為盛焉。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, among all examination categories, Jinshi was especially honored, and its yield of talent was also the most abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Among all examination tracks, Jinshi was the most prestigious and produced the greatest number of outstanding officials.

sentences.zh: 方其取以辭章，類若浮文而少實；

translations.literal: When they were selected by literary composition, it seemed like floating writing with little substance;
translations.idiomatic: When selected by literary composition alone, candidates seemed skilled in surface rhetoric but thin on substance;

sentences.zh: 及其臨事設施，奮其事業，隱然為國名臣者，不可勝數，遂使時君篤意，以謂莫此之尚。

translations.literal: yet when they faced affairs and put measures into practice, striving in their careers, those who quietly became famed ministers of the state were beyond counting, so that rulers of the time devoted their intent, holding that nothing surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: yet in office countless Jinshi graduates became renowned statesmen, so emperors came to regard no track as superior.

sentences.zh: 及其後世，俗益媮薄，上下交疑，因以謂按其聲病，可以為有司之責，舍是則汗漫而無所守，遂不復能易。

translations.literal: In later generations customs grew increasingly lax and shallow, superiors and subordinates mutually suspicious; therefore it was held that checking tonal faults could serve as the responsibility of the offices—in abandoning this there was only vagueness with nothing to uphold, and it could no longer be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages grew lax; rulers and candidates grew suspicious of one another. Examiners clung to tonal rules as their only standard, fearing that without them selection would lack all discipline—and the system could no longer be reformed.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，乃知三代鄉里德行之舉，非至治之隆莫能行也。

translations.literal: Alas—thus one knows that the village and district selection by virtue of the Three Dynasties could be practiced only under the loftiest age of perfect governance.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—only under the loftiest age of perfect governance could the Three Dynasties' village selection by moral conduct have been sustained.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，冀州進士張昌齡、王公謹有名于當時，考功員外郎王師旦不署以第。

translations.literal: Under Taizong, Jizhou Jinshi Zhang Changling and Wang Gongjin were famed in their time, but Vice Director of Personnel Wang Shidan did not certify them with a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, the celebrated Jizhou Jinshi Zhang Changling and Wang Gongjin were denied grades by Vice Director Wang Shidan.

sentences.zh: 太宗問其故，對曰：「二人者，皆文采浮華，擢之將誘後生而弊風俗。

translations.literal: Taizong asked the reason; he replied: "These two men are both florid in literary ornament; promoting them would entice later students and harm custom."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked why. Wang replied: "Both men write florid, ornamental prose. Promoting them would mislead later candidates and corrupt public morals."

sentences.zh: 」其後，二人者卒不能有立。

translations.literal: " Afterward, the two men in the end achieved no lasting standing.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end, neither man achieved lasting distinction.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，禮部侍郎楊綰上疏言：「進士科起于隋大業中，是時猶試策。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying, Vice Minister of Rites Yang Guan submitted a memorial stating: "The Jinshi examination arose in the Daye era of Sui, when policy questions were still tested."
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying year 2, Vice Minister Yang Guan memorialized: "The Jinshi track began in Sui's Daye era, when candidates still answered policy questions."

sentences.zh: 高宗朝，劉思立加進士雜文，明經填帖，故為進士者皆誦當代之文，而不通經史，明經者但記帖括。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong, Liu Sili added belles-lettres for Jinshi and fill-in text-slips for Mingjing; therefore Jinshi candidates all recited contemporary writings without mastering classics and histories, while Mingjing candidates merely memorized slip formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Liu Sili added belles-lettres for Jinshi and fill-in slips for Mingjing, so Jinshi candidates memorized contemporary essays without mastering classics, and Mingjing candidates memorized slip formulas alone.

sentences.zh: 又投牒自舉，非古先哲王側席待賢之道。

translations.literal: Moreover, presenting credentials to nominate oneself is not the way of ancient sage-kings who vacated their seats awaiting the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Self-nomination by credential is not how ancient sage-kings vacated their thrones to await worthy men.

sentences.zh: 請依古察孝廉，其鄉閭孝友、信義、廉恥而通經者，縣薦之州，州試其所通之學，送於省。

translations.literal: I request following antiquity in investigating Filial and Incorrupt candidates: those in their villages filial and friendly, faithful and righteous, knowing shame and mastering classics—the county recommends to the prefecture, the prefecture tests what they have mastered, and sends them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the ancient Filial and Incorrupt investigation: men known in their villages for filial piety, friendship, faithfulness, righteousness, integrity, and classical learning should be recommended by counties, tested by prefectures, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 自縣至省，皆勿自投牒，其到狀、保辨、識牒皆停。

translations.literal: From county to capital, none should present credentials on their own; arrival memorials, guarantee verification, and identification documents should all be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: From county to capital, self-presentation should end; arrival memorials, guarantees, and identification papers should all be abolished.

sentences.zh: 而所習經，取大義，聽通諸家之學。

translations.literal: For classics studied, major principles were taken, and mastery of various schools' learning was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Classics should be tested on major principles, allowing mastery across schools of interpretation.

sentences.zh: 每問經十條，對策三道，皆通，為上第，吏部官之；

translations.literal: Ten questions on classics and three policy answers each time—all passing ranked upper grade, with the Ministry of Personnel appointing office;
translations.idiomatic: Ten classic questions and three policy answers: full passage earned upper grade and appointment by the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 經義通八，策通二，為中第，與出身；

translations.literal: eight classics and two policy questions passed ranked middle grade, granting examination credentials;
translations.idiomatic: eight classics and two policy passes earned middle grade and examination credentials;

sentences.zh: 下第，罷歸。

translations.literal: lower grade, dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: lower grade meant dismissal.

sentences.zh: 《論語》、《孝經》、《孟子》兼為一經，其明經、進士及道舉並停。」

translations.literal: The Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, and Mencius together counted as one classic; Mingjing, Jinshi, and the Daoist recommendation track should all be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects, Filial Piety Classic, and Mencius together should count as one classic; Mingjing, Jinshi, and the Daoist track should all be abolished."

sentences.zh: 詔給事中李棲筠、李廙、尚書左丞賈至、京兆尹兼御史大夫嚴武議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Investigation and Remonstrance Attendant Li Qiyun, Li Yi, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao Intendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Yan Wu to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Attendants Li Qiyun and Li Yi, Assistant Director Jia Zhi, and Jingzhao Intendant Yan Wu to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 棲筠等議曰：

translations.literal: Li Qiyun and the others deliberated, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun and his colleagues replied:

sentences.zh: 「夏之政忠，商之政敬，周之政文，然則文與忠敬皆統人行。

translations.literal: "The government of Xia was marked by sincerity, that of Shang by reverence, that of Zhou by culture—thus culture together with sincerity and reverence all govern human conduct."
translations.idiomatic: "Xia government embodied sincerity, Shang reverence, Zhou culture—culture, sincerity, and reverence together govern human conduct."

sentences.zh: 且諡號述行，莫美于文，文興則忠敬存焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, posthumous titles describe conduct, and nothing is finer than culture; when culture flourishes, sincerity and reverence are preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles describe a life's conduct, and nothing surpasses culture; when culture flourishes, sincerity and reverence endure.

sentences.zh: 故前代以文取士，本文行也，由辭觀行，則及辭焉。

translations.literal: Therefore former ages selected officials by literary culture—this was rooted in conduct; observing conduct through literary expression, one thereby reaches the expression itself.
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties selected officials through literary culture because culture reflects conduct; to read conduct through words is to value the words themselves.

sentences.zh: 宣父稱顏子「不遷怒，不貳過」，謂之「好學」。

translations.literal: The Master called Yan Hui "not transferring anger, not repeating faults," terming this "fond of learning."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised Yan Hui for "not transferring anger, not repeating the same fault," and called this true love of learning.

sentences.zh: 今試學者以帖字為精通，不窮旨義，豈能知遷怒、貳過之道乎？

translations.literal: Now students are tested on text-slip characters as mastery without exhausting principles and meanings—how can they know the way of not transferring anger or repeating faults?
translations.idiomatic: Today students are tested on memorized text-slips without probing meaning—how can they grasp not transferring anger or repeating faults?

sentences.zh: 考文者以聲病為是非，豈能知移風易俗化天下乎？

translations.literal: Those examining belles-lettres take tonal faults as right and wrong—how can they know transforming customs and changing popular practice to civilize the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Examiners judge essays by tonal rules—how can they identify those who would transform customs and civilize the realm?

sentences.zh: 是以上失其源，下襲其流，先王之道莫能行也。

translations.literal: Thus superiors have lost the source, subordinates have followed the current, and the way of former kings cannot be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors have lost the source, subordinates follow the drift, and the way of the ancient kings cannot be practiced.

sentences.zh: 夫先王之道消，則小人之道長，亂臣賊子由是生焉！

translations.literal: When the way of former kings fades, the way of petty men grows long—rebellious ministers and unfilial sons are thereby born!
translations.idiomatic: When the way of the ancient kings fades, petty men flourish—and rebellious ministers and unfilial sons arise!

sentences.zh: 今取士試之小道，而不以遠大，是猶以蝸蚓之餌垂海，而望吞舟之魚，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: Now in recruiting officials petty paths are tested, not the far-reaching and great—this is like dangling snail-and-worm bait over the sea and hoping for fish that swallow boats—is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Testing petty skills instead of great capacity is like dangling worm bait over the ocean and expecting leviathans—is that not futile?

sentences.zh: 所以食垂餌者皆小魚，就科目者皆小藝。

translations.literal: Those who eat dangling bait are all small fish; those who pursue examination categories are all petty arts.
translations.idiomatic: Only small fish take dangling bait; only petty skills win examination categories.

sentences.zh: 且夏有天下四百載，禹之道喪而商始興；

translations.literal: Moreover, Xia held the realm four hundred years; when Yu's way was lost Shang first rose;
translations.idiomatic: Xia ruled four hundred years; when Yu's way faded, Shang rose;

sentences.zh: 商有天下六百祀，湯之法棄而周始興；

translations.literal: Shang held the realm six hundred reign-years; when Tang's methods were abandoned Zhou first rose;
translations.idiomatic: Shang endured six hundred years; when Tang's methods were abandoned, Zhou rose;

sentences.zh: 周有天下八百年，文、武之政廢而秦始並焉。

translations.literal: Zhou held the realm eight hundred years; when the government of Wen and Wu was abandoned Qin first united it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lasted eight hundred years; when the governments of Wen and Wu collapsed, Qin united the realm.

sentences.zh: 三代之選士任賢，皆考實行，是以風俗淳一，運祚長遠。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties in selecting scholars and appointing the worthy all examined actual conduct; therefore customs were pure and unified, and fortune's span was long and far.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties selected talent by examining real conduct, so customs stayed pure and dynasties endured.

sentences.zh: 漢興，監其然，尊儒術，尚名節，雖近戚竊位，強臣擅權，弱主外立，母后專政，而亦能終彼四百，豈非學行之效邪？

translations.literal: When Han arose, observing this pattern, it honored Confucian learning and prized reputation and integrity; though close kin usurped position, powerful ministers monopolized authority, weak rulers were installed from outside, and empress dowagers held government—yet it could also complete those four hundred years—is this not the effect of learning and conduct?
translations.idiomatic: Han observed this lesson, honored Confucian learning, and prized integrity. Though kin usurped power, strong ministers dominated, weak emperors were installed, and empress dowagers ruled, the dynasty still lasted four centuries—is that not the fruit of learning and moral conduct?

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，專尚浮侈，德義不修，故子孫速顛，享國不永也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, floating extravagance alone was honored and virtue and righteousness were not cultivated; therefore descendants quickly toppled and enjoyment of the realm was not long.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, extravagance alone was prized and virtue neglected, so dynasties fell swiftly and ruled briefly.

sentences.zh: 今綰所請，實為正論。

translations.literal: What Guan now requests is truly correct doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan's proposal is fundamentally sound.

sentences.zh: 然自晉室之亂，南北分裂，人多僑處，必欲復古鄉舉裏選，竊恐未盡。

translations.literal: Yet since the disorder of the Jin house, north and south were divided and many people sojourned abroad; if one must restore ancient village presentation and district selection, I fear privately it may not be fully feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Jin's collapse and the north-south split, many people live far from home; restoring ancient village and district selection may not be fully feasible.

sentences.zh: 請兼廣學校，以明訓誘。

translations.literal: I request also broadly expanding schools to clarify instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: We ask instead to expand schools and strengthen instruction.

sentences.zh: 雖京師州縣皆有小學，兵革之後，生徒流離，儒臣、師氏，祿廩無向。

translations.literal: Though capital and prefectures and counties all have elementary schools, after arms and campaigns students have scattered, Confucian officials and masters have had no direction for salary and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Though elementary schools exist in capital and provinces alike, war has scattered students and left teachers without salaries or supplies.

sentences.zh: 請增博士員，厚其稟稍，選通儒碩生，間居其職。

translations.literal: I request increasing erudite posts, enriching their stipends, and selecting broadly learned eminent scholars to fill these positions in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Increase erudite posts, enrich stipends, and appoint distinguished Confucian scholars to fill them in rotation.

sentences.zh: 十道大郡，置太學館，遣博士出外，兼領郡官，以教生徒。

translations.literal: In the ten circuits' great prefectures, establish Imperial College halls, send erudites outward who concurrently head prefectural office to teach students.
translations.idiomatic: In major prefectures of the ten circuits, establish Imperial College halls, send erudites to teach while concurrently holding prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 保桑梓者，鄉里舉焉；

translations.literal: Those who preserve their native place should be recommended by village and district;
translations.idiomatic: Those who remain in their home districts should be recommended locally;

sentences.zh: 在流寓者，庠序推焉。

translations.literal: those sojourning abroad should be promoted by the schools.
translations.idiomatic: those living abroad should be nominated by their schools.

sentences.zh: 朝而行之，夕見其利。」

translations.literal: Implement it in the morning and see its benefit by evening."
translations.idiomatic: Adopt this in the morning and see its benefit by evening."

sentences.zh: 而大臣以為舉人循習，難於速變，請自來歲始。

translations.literal: But the great ministers held that candidates were accustomed to established practice and rapid change was difficult; they requested implementation from the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers argued that candidates were too entrenched in current practice for sudden change and asked to begin the following year.

sentences.zh: 帝以問翰林學士，對曰：「舉進士久矣，廢之恐失其業。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Hanlin Academicians, who replied: "Jinshi candidacy has long existed; abolishing it may cause them to lose their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hanlin academicians, who replied: "The Jinshi track has existed for generations; abolishing it would deprive many of their livelihood."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔明經、進士與孝廉兼行。

translations.literal: " An edict therefore ordered Mingjing, Jinshi, and Filial and Incorrupt to proceed together.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered Mingjing, Jinshi, and Filial and Incorrupt tracks to continue side by side.

sentences.zh: 先是，進士試詩、賦及時務策五道，明經策三道。

translations.literal: Previously, Jinshi were tested on poetry, rhapsody, and five current-affairs policy questions; Mingjing on three policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Jinshi took poetry, rhapsody, and five policy questions; Mingjing took three.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，中書舍人趙贊權知貢舉，乃以箴、論、表、贊代詩、賦，而皆試策三道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Secretariat Drafter Zhao Zan as acting overseer of tribute presentation substituted admonitions, discourses, memorials, and encomia for poetry and rhapsody, while all were tested on three policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 2, Acting Presentation Overseer Zhao Zan replaced poetry and rhapsody with admonitions, discourses, memorials, and encomia, while all candidates took three policy questions.

sentences.zh: 大和八年，禮部復罷進士議論，而試詩、賦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dahe, the Ministry of Rites again suspended Jinshi discourses and tested poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe year 8, Rites again dropped Jinshi discourses and restored poetry and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 文宗從內出題以試進士，謂侍臣曰：「吾患文格浮薄，昨自出題，所試差勝。

translations.literal: Wenzong issued examination topics from within the palace to test Jinshi, telling attending ministers: "I worry that literary standards are shallow and thin; yesterday, setting topics myself, those tested were somewhat better."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong set Jinshi topics himself from within the palace and told his ministers: "I worry that literary standards have grown shallow; when I set the topics yesterday, the results were somewhat better."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔禮部歲取登第者三十人，苟無其人，不必充其數。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered the Ministry of Rites to take thirty who passed each year; if there were no such persons, the quota need not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Rites to pass thirty Jinshi each year, without filling the quota if qualified candidates were lacking.

sentences.zh: 是時，文宗好學嗜古，鄭覃以經術位宰相，深嫉進士浮薄，屢請罷之。

translations.literal: At this time Wenzong loved learning and cherished antiquity; Zheng Tan, by classical learning attaining the chancellorship, deeply resented the shallowness of Jinshi and repeatedly requested their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved learning and antiquity; Chancellor Zheng Tan, a classicist, despised the Jinshi track's shallowness and repeatedly petitioned to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「敦厚浮薄，色色有之，進士科取人二百年矣，不可遽廢。

translations.literal: Wenzong said: "The solid and the shallow exist in every category; the Jinshi examination has recruited talent for two hundred years—it cannot be abruptly abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong replied: "Integrity and shallowness appear in every walk of life. The Jinshi track has selected talent for two centuries—it cannot be abolished overnight."

sentences.zh: 」因得不罷。

translations.literal: " Therefore it was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The track was therefore spared.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，宰相李德裕尤惡進士。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, Chancellor Li Deyu especially detested Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong succeeded, Chancellor Li Deyu especially despised the Jinshi track.

sentences.zh: 初，舉人既及第，綴行通名，詣主司第謝。

translations.literal: Initially, once candidates had passed, they formed a procession announcing names and went to the chief examiner's residence to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: After passing, candidates formed a procession, announced their names, and visited the chief examiner's home to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 其制，序立西階下，北上東向；

translations.literal: By regulation they lined up below the western steps, proceeding north and facing east;
translations.idiomatic: By regulation they lined up below the western steps, facing north and east;

sentences.zh: 主人席東階下。

translations.literal: the host was seated below the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: the host sat below the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 西向；

translations.literal: Facing west;
translations.idiomatic: Facing west;

sentences.zh: 諸生拜，主司答拜；

translations.literal: the students bowed, the chief examiner returned the bow;
translations.idiomatic: students bowed and the examiner returned the bow;

sentences.zh: 乃敘齒，謝恩，遂升階，與公卿觀者皆坐；

translations.literal: then they ordered by seniority, thanked for grace, ascended the steps, and both grandees and onlookers were seated;
translations.idiomatic: they then took seats by seniority, expressed gratitude, ascended the steps, and grandees and onlookers sat down;

sentences.zh: 酒數行，乃赴期集。

translations.literal: after several rounds of wine they proceeded to the scheduled gathering.
translations.idiomatic: after several rounds of wine they went on to the scheduled gathering.

sentences.zh: 又有曲江會、題名席。

translations.literal: There were also the Qujiang gathering and the inscription banquet.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Qujiang gathering and the inscription banquet.

sentences.zh: 至是，德裕奏：「國家設科取士，而附黨背公，自為門生。

translations.literal: At this point Deyu memorialized: "The state established examinations to recruit scholars, yet they attach to factions, turn their backs on the public good, and make themselves private disciples."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu then memorialized: "The state established examinations to recruit talent, yet graduates attach to factions, betray the public interest, and form private patronage circles."

sentences.zh: 自今一見有司而止，其期集、參謁、曲江題名皆罷。

translations.literal: From now on they should see the responsible offices once and stop; scheduled gatherings, courtesy calls, and Qujiang inscription were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth candidates were to visit the responsible offices once only; scheduled gatherings, courtesy calls, and Qujiang inscription banquets were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 」德裕嘗論公卿子弟艱于科舉，武宗曰：「向聞楊虞卿兄弟朋比貴勢，妨平進之路。

translations.literal: " Deyu once discussed how sons of grandees and ministers found the civil examinations difficult; Wuzong said: "I have heard that the brothers Yang Yuqing formed factions with the powerful and noble, obstructing the path of fair advancement."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Deyu once argued that sons of high officials struggled in the examinations. Wuzong replied: "I have heard that the Yang Yuqing brothers formed factions with powerful families and blocked fair advancement."

sentences.zh: 昨黜楊知至、鄭樸等，抑其太甚耳。

translations.literal: Yesterday Yang Zhizhi, Zheng Pu, and others were dismissed—merely restraining them when they went too far.
translations.idiomatic: I dismissed Yang Zhizhi, Zheng Pu, and others only to restrain excess, not to exclude all high-born candidates.

sentences.zh: 有司不識朕意，不放子弟，即過矣，但取實藝可也。

translations.literal: If responsible offices do not understand my intent and do not admit sons of officials, that is going too far; they need only select genuine talent.
translations.idiomatic: If examiners misunderstand my intent and bar all officials' sons, that goes too far—they need only select genuine ability.

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「鄭肅、封敖子弟皆有才，不敢應舉。

translations.literal: " Deyu said: "The sons of Zheng Su and Feng Ao all have talent but dare not take the examinations."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Deyu said: "The sons of Zheng Su and Feng Ao are talented but dare not sit for the examinations."

sentences.zh: 臣無名第，不當非進士。

translations.literal: I have no examination rank and should not disparage Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: I hold no examination degree myself and should not disparage the Jinshi track.

sentences.zh: 然臣祖天寶末以仕進無他岐，勉強隨計，一舉登第。

translations.literal: Yet my grandfather at the end of Tianbao, with no other path to office advancement, reluctantly followed the annual presentation and passed in a single attempt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the end of Tianbao my grandfather, with no other path to office, reluctantly took the examination and passed on the first try.

sentences.zh: 自後家不置《文選》，蓋惡其不根藝實。

translations.literal: Afterward our family did not keep the Wenxuan, hating that it was not rooted in genuine artistic substance.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward our family kept no copy of the Wenxuan, despising its lack of grounding in real learning.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷顯官，須公卿子弟為之。

translations.literal: Yet prominent offices at court must be filled by sons of grandees and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prominent court offices must be filled by sons of grandees and ministers.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 少習其業，目熟朝廷事，台閣之儀，不教而自成。

translations.literal: From youth they practice that profession, their eyes familiar with court affairs, the etiquette of the terrace and pavilion—formed without teaching.
translations.idiomatic: From youth they practice statecraft, grow familiar with court affairs and terrace etiquette, and master protocol without formal instruction.
