sentences.zh: 寒士縱有出人之才，固不能閑習也。

translations.literal: Poor scholars, though they may have outstanding talent, truly cannot practice these at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Poor scholars, however gifted, cannot acquire such familiarity in their spare time.

sentences.zh: 則子弟未易可輕。

translations.literal: Thus sons of officials are not easily to be slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' sons therefore should not be lightly dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」德裕之論，偏異蓋如此。

translations.literal: " Deyu's argument was partial and unusual in roughly this way.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Deyu's argument was partial and idiosyncratic in roughly this way.

sentences.zh: 然進士科當唐之晚節，尤為浮薄，世所共患也。

translations.literal: Yet the Jinshi examination in the late phase of Tang was especially shallow and thin—a common affliction of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in late Tang the Jinshi track had grown especially shallow—an affliction universally lamented.

sentences.zh: 所謂制舉者，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: What is called the zhiju examination—its origin is distant indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The zhiju (special summons) examination dates back to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，天子常稱制詔道其所欲問而親策之。

translations.literal: From Han onward, the Son of Heaven often issued edicts in his own name stating what he wished to ask and personally examined candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times, emperors often issued edicts in their own name stating what they wished to ask and personally examined candidates.

sentences.zh: 唐興，世崇儒學，雖其時君賢愚好惡不同，而樂善求賢之意未始少怠，故自京師外至州縣，有司常選之士，以時而舉。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, the age honored Confucian learning; though rulers differed in wisdom and folly and in likes and dislikes, the intent to delight in goodness and seek the worthy never slackened, so from the capital outward to prefectures and counties, responsible offices regularly selected scholars and presented them according to the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang rose, the age honored Confucian learning; though emperors differed in wisdom and taste, the will to seek worthy men never slackened, and offices from the capital to every prefecture presented talent on schedule.

sentences.zh: 而天子又自詔四方德行、才能、文學之士，或高蹈幽隱與其不能自達者，下至軍謀將略、翹關拔山、絕藝奇伎莫不兼取。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also by his own edict summoned from the four directions men of virtue and conduct, talent and ability, and literary culture—whether lofty in conduct and secluded in retirement or unable to advance themselves—down to military strategy and generalship, gate-lifting and mountain-pulling, and extraordinary arts and rare skills, all were taken together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors also summoned by edict men of virtue, talent, and letters from every direction—including recluses who could not advance themselves—along with strategists, strongmen, and masters of rare skills.

sentences.zh: 其為名目，隨其人主臨時所欲，而列為定科者，如賢良方正、直言極諫、博通墳典達於教化、軍謀宏遠堪任將率、詳明政術可以理人之類，其名最著。

translations.literal: Their designations followed what each ruler temporarily desired; those listed as fixed categories included Filial and Incorrupt, Direct Remonstrance, Broad Mastery of Canonical Texts Reaching to Transformation through Teaching, Grand Military Strategy Fit to Command Generals, and Detailed Clarity in Governmental Arts Able to Govern People—these names were most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Categories varied with each emperor's wishes; fixed tracks included Filial and Incorrupt, Direct Remonstrance, Broad Mastery of the Classics, Grand Military Strategy, and Clarity in Governmental Arts—the best-known designations.

sentences.zh: 而天子巡狩、行幸、封禪太山梁父，往往會見行在，其所以待之之禮甚優，而宏材偉論非常之人亦時出於其間，不為無得也。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven toured, traveled, or performed feng and shan rites on Mount Tai and Liangfu, they often met at the traveling palace; the courtesy with which they were received was very generous, and great talents with lofty discourse and extraordinary men also emerged among them from time to time—it was not without gain.
translations.idiomatic: When emperors toured the realm or performed feng and shan rites on Mount Tai and Liangfu, candidates often met them at the traveling palace and were treated with great honor; outstanding men of exceptional ability sometimes emerged—so the system was not without merit.

sentences.zh: 其外，又有武舉，蓋其起于武后之時。

translations.literal: Besides these, there was also the military examination, which arose roughly in the time of Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a military examination track, which arose under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，始置武舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, the military examination was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an year 2, the military examination was formally established.

sentences.zh: 其制，有長垛、馬射、步射、平射、筒射，又有馬槍、翹關、負重、身材之選。

translations.literal: Its regulations included long rampart shooting, mounted archery, foot archery, level shooting, and tube shooting; also mounted lance, gate-lifting, weight-bearing, and physique selection.
translations.idiomatic: Tests included long-range archery, mounted and foot archery, level and tube shooting, mounted lance, gate-lifting, weight-bearing, and physique assessment.

sentences.zh: 翹關，長丈七尺，徑三寸半，凡十舉後，手持關距，出處無過一尺；

translations.literal: For gate-lifting, the pole was one zhang and seven chi long, three and a half cun in diameter; after ten lifts, holding the pole at the grip, the rise and fall might not exceed one chi;
translations.idiomatic: In gate-lifting, candidates raised a pole one zhang seven chi long and three and a half cun thick; after ten lifts, the pole's rise and fall at the grip could not exceed one chi;

sentences.zh: 負重者，負米五斛，行二十步：皆為中第，亦以鄉飲酒禮送兵部。

translations.literal: for weight-bearing, carrying five hu of grain and walking twenty paces—all ranked as middle grade, and also sent to the Ministry of War with the village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: in weight-bearing, carrying five hu of grain twenty paces—all counted as a pass, and candidates were sent to the Ministry of War with the village drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其選用之法不足道，故不復書。

translations.literal: The methods of their selection and appointment are not worth recounting, and therefore are not recorded further.
translations.idiomatic: Their appointment procedures are not worth recounting and are therefore omitted.
